property_summary: For any caller and any amounts/timestamps, calling Collect does not change the ability of the contract to accept a subsequent zero-value Put call (i.e. the reference accepts msg.value==0 in Put so a zero-value call succeeds after Collect), but the mutant blocks zero-value deposits (requires msg.value>0) so some sequences where a caller does a Collect then attempts a zero-value Put will succeed on reference and fail on mutant.

For any caller, performing Collect(...) never prevents that same caller can subsequently call Put(0) with msg.value == 0 on the reference (it accepts zero-value Put), whereas the mutant disallows zero-value Put and thus will revert such a call for some fuzzed inputs.

For any caller and amounts/timestamps, calling Collect(...) does not change that the reference contract accepts a subsequent zero-value Put(0) (i.e. Put with msg.value == 0 always succeeds on the reference), whereas the mutant rejects zero-value Put calls (requires msg.value > 0), so a sequence Collect(...) then Put(0) succeeds on the reference for all inputs but can revert on the mutant for some inputs.

For any actor, after any sequence, calling Put with msg.value == 0 always succeeds on the reference (Put allows zero-value deposits), but the mutant rejects zero-value Put (requires msg.value > 0) so a zero-value Put by any caller may revert on the mutant.

For any caller/amount/unlockTime, calling Collect(...) on the reference never prevents that same caller can subsequently perform a zero-value fallback/send (i.e., address(c).balance does not block a zero-value fallback-triggered Put), whereas the mutant that requires msg.value>0 in Put will revert on a zero-value call — so the rule: a zero-value external call to the contract (which routes to Put via fallback) always succeeds on the reference; the mutant rejects some such calls.

For any caller and any _unlockTime and msg.value, after Put returns the stored unlockTime is never less than block.timestamp (i.e., acc.unlockTime >= block.timestamp); the mutant that assigns acc.unlockTime = _unlockTime can set unlockTime < block.timestamp and thus violate this invariant for some inputs.

After any call to Put by any address with any _unlockTime and any msg.value, the stored unlockTime for that address is always >= the block.timestamp at the time of the call; the mutant that assigns acc.unlockTime = _unlockTime can set it below block.timestamp for some inputs, violating this invariant.

For any caller, after Put(...) returns the stored unlockTime for that caller is at least the block.timestamp at the time of the call (the reference enforces max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp)); the mutant that assigns unlockTime = _unlockTime can make it less than block.timestamp for some fuzzed _unlockTime values, violating this rule.

For any Put(...) call, if the caller provides _unlockTime that is >= current block.timestamp then the stored unlockTime equals that _unlockTime; the mutant that unconditionally assigns _unlockTime can break this by setting a stored unlockTime less than block.timestamp for some inputs where _unlockTime < block.timestamp, but those are excluded by the admissible domain—so we instead assert that when _unlockTime >= block.timestamp, stored unlockTime == _unlockTime (reference preserves, mutant may still set arbitrary value only when _unlockTime < block.timestamp).

For any caller and any Put(...) call, if the caller supplies _unlockTime less than or equal to the current block.timestamp then the contract will store acc.unlockTime equal to block.timestamp (i.e., it never decreases below block.timestamp); the mutant that assigns acc.unlockTime = _unlockTime can set it below block.timestamp for some fuzzed inputs, violating this rule.

For any caller and any sent value, calling Put(...) on the correct contract increases (or preserves) that caller's recorded Acc[msg.sender].balance by exactly the msg.value added to the previous stored balance; the mutant overwrites the stored balance with msg.value, so there exist inputs where the resulting stored balance is smaller than the previous balance plus msg.value.

For any caller and any sent value, calling Put(...) preserves the invariant that Acc[caller].balance after the call equals the previous Acc[caller].balance plus msg.value; the mutant that sets acc.balance = msg.value can make the post-call balance smaller than the previous balance plus msg.value for some inputs (when previous balance nonzero).

For any caller and any sent msg.value, calling Put(...) on the reference contract always makes Acc[caller].balance equal to its previous balance plus msg.value; the mutant that sets acc.balance = msg.value can make the post-call balance smaller than previous+msg.value when the caller already had a nonzero balance.

For any caller and any sent non-negative value, after calling Put(...) the contract's public Acc(caller).balance is at least as large as the msg.value sent in that call; the mutant that overwrites the balance with msg.value can make the post-call balance smaller than msg.value when the prior stored balance was greater than msg.value, so it violates this rule for some inputs.

For any caller and any msg.value, calling Put(_) on the reference contract results in Acc[caller].balance being at least max(previous_balance, msg.value) (i.e., it never decreases below the previous stored balance nor below the sent value); the mutant that overwrites acc.balance = msg.value can make the post-call balance smaller than the previous balance when previous_balance > msg.value.

For any caller and any positive payable amount sent to Put, the Log contract records a message whose Val equals the actual msg.value sent; the mutant records double the value for some inputs, violating this equality.

After any call to Put by any payer with any amount, the Log.LastMsg.Val equals the actual ether value sent; the mutant that logs msg.value*2 will cause LastMsg.Val != sent value for some inputs.

For every call to Put by any sender sending any nonnegative ether amount, the Log.LastMsg.Val recorded by C equals the actual msg.value sent; the mutant that logs msg.value*2 will make this equality false for some inputs.

For any caller and any supplied _unlockTime, after calling Put with a positive deposit the stored unlockTime is at least the supplied _unlockTime if the supplied _unlockTime is in the future (i.e., acc.unlockTime >= _unlockTime when _unlockTime > block.timestamp); the mutant that always sets acc.unlockTime = block.timestamp can make acc.unlockTime < _unlockTime for some future _unlockTime, breaking this rule.

For any caller and any supplied _unlockTime, after calling Put with a positive msg.value the stored acc.unlockTime is at least block.timestamp and equals max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp); the mutant that always sets acc.unlockTime = block.timestamp can violate the relation acc.unlockTime >= _unlockTime when _unlockTime > block.timestamp.
